steps.name: Preranked GSEA on the full tested list (Wald statistic)
caveats: ORA and preranked GSEA on the same data routinely return different set lists; neither is the truth and the disagreement itself must be reported
Hallmark sets are broad and overlapping; a Hallmark hit is a pointer to a programme, not a specific pathway
steps.context: This is the guard on T2S1. An over-representation test discards every gene below the cutoff, and with 12 samples the cutoff may leave too few genes for a hypergeometric test to have power. A preranked test uses the whole list and detects a set whose members all shift a little without any single member reaching significance. It is also the honest way to show how much of the ORA answer is an artefact of where the threshold was placed. The disputed choice of ranking statistic is settled here in favour of the DESeq2 Wald statistic: it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, whereas the unshrunken log2 fold change is noisy for low-count genes and a signed p-value produces ties wherever p saturates.

plan.title: AD lesional vs control GO-BP over-representation
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question is narrow: which GO biological processes are over-represented among the genes called significant in the treated (AD lesional) versus control contrast. A DESeq2 results table for that contrast is already supplied (/data/inputs/results/de_results.csv, 12000 genes x 8 columns), so no differential expression needs to be re-run — the plan starts from that table. Three things still have to be settled before an over-representation test can be trusted, and they set the step order.

T1S1 triages the supplied results table and the counts/metadata that accompany it (12000 x 13 counts from Salmon, 12 samples, 6 treated vs 6 control, single batch). It fixes the significance cutoff (padj < 0.05, Benjamini-Hochberg), counts how many genes pass, separates NA padj coming from DESeq2 Cook's-distance outlier flagging from NA coming from independent filtering, inspects the raw p-value histogram (a non-uniform null makes the adjusted p-values, and therefore the gene list, untrustworthy), and reports sample_01 — flagged in the profile at ~4x below median library size — on a blind-vst PCA and a sample-distance heatmap. sample_01 is kept unless there is a stated reason beyond depth; size factors already account for depth. This step also defines the universe: the genes actually tested (non-NA padj), not the whole annotation, since a whole-genome universe would report the skin transcriptome back as an enrichment.

T2S1 is the answer to the question: enrichGO over the GO Biological Process branch, human, with the tested genes as universe, symbols mapped to Entrez with org.Hs.eg.db and the unmapped share reported, set size restricted to 15-500 genes after intersection with the universe, BH adjustment, and rrvgo semantic-similarity reduction of the significant terms to representatives (GO BP is a nested hierarchy — parent and child terms share members, so an uncollapsed list of 200 terms is not 200 findings). Because these are count data from Salmon, the significant list is biased toward long and highly expressed genes; the step runs goseq with a gene-length probability weighting function as a bias-corrected companion where effective lengths are recoverable, and states plainly if they are not. Up- and down-regulated genes are tested separately as well as jointly, since opposite-direction processes cancel in a combined list.

T2S2 is the guard against the single largest failure mode of an over-representation test: if fewer than ~50 genes pass padj < 0.05, a hypergeometric test on that list has no power and the result would swing with the threshold. It runs fgsea preranked on the full tested list, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic — the disputed ranking-metric choice is settled here in favour of the Wald stat, because it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, unlike the unshrunken fold change (noisy at low counts) or a signed p-value (ties at saturation). It covers GO BP and Hallmark. If the ORA list is large this is a concordance check; if it is short, this becomes the primary result and the report says so.

T1S3 assembles the report: representative GO BP terms with their gene members, the full table as a supplement, leading-edge genes per significant GSEA set, and the reproducibility record — collection version (MSigDB 2026.1 / GO.db 3.23.1), package versions, seed, universe, size window, ranking metric. It states the method-dependence caveat explicitly: ORA and preranked GSEA on the same data give different lists, and an enriched term is a hypothesis for follow-up, not a demonstrated mechanism.

The ranking metric is the DESeq2 Wald statistic and this choice is stated in the output
Set size window 15-500 applied after intersection with the ranked list; the seed is set and recorded
Results reported for GO BP and Hallmark separately with NES and BH-adjusted p
Leading-edge genes are listed per significant set, with overlap between sets marked
Overlap and disagreement with the T2S1 enrichGO representatives is tabulated explicitly
Gene set collection name and release version are recorded
constraints: enrichment: gsea_input = full ranked list of tested genes — never a thresholded list
enrichment: rank_metric = stat (DESeq2 Wald statistic); rank_metric_not = unshrunken log2 fold change alone, signed p-value with ties
enrichment: rank_metric_choice is stated explicitly in the plan and in the report
enrichment: min_size = 15, max_size = 500 after intersection with the ranked list
enrichment: gene_set_collection = human hallmark, plus human GO BP as the ontology-level pass; state each release
Set and record a random seed for the fgsea permutations
Verify the human gene set collections are present before use; never run a mouse collection against human symbols
caveats: ORA and preranked GSEA on the same data routinely return different set lists; neither is the truth and the disagreement itself must be reported
Hallmark sets are broad and overlapping; a Hallmark hit is a pointer to a programme, not a specific pathway

steps.name: Enrichment report with reproducibility record
steps.question: What are the representative over-represented GO biological processes in atopic dermatitis lesional vs control skin, how robust are they to method choice, and under what parameters were they obtained?
steps.description: Assemble a single report from T1S1, T2S1 and T2S2. Lead with the representative GO Biological Process terms over-represented among the significant genes, with their member genes, effect direction, and adjusted p-values, and state the size of the significant gene list that produced them. Include the full unreduced enrichGO table as a supplement, the leading-edge genes of each significant preranked set, and the ORA-vs-GSEA concordance table. Record for reproducibility: sessionInfo, package versions, the random seed used for the permutations, the gene set collection and annotation release versions, the universe definition and its size, the gene set size window, the significance cutoffs, and the ranking metric. State the method-dependence caveat explicitly, and state the sample_01 depth caveat and the p-value histogram verdict from T1S1. Present enriched terms as hypotheses for follow-up, not as demonstrated mechanism.
steps.context: The user asked a single question — which GO biological processes are over-represented. The report must answer it directly and then qualify it honestly: with 6 vs 6 samples and a 12000-gene table, the significant list drives everything downstream, and the enrichment result is a function of the cutoff, the universe, the collection version and the test chosen. Every one of those has to be on the page for the answer to be reusable.
acceptance_criteria: Representative GO BP terms are presented first, with member genes, direction and adjusted p-values
The number of genes in the significant list is stated alongside the enrichment result
Universe definition and size, gene set size window, significance cutoffs, ranking metric, collection and annotation versions are all recorded
Leading-edge genes are listed per significant preranked set
The ORA vs preranked GSEA disagreement is reported rather than reconciled away
sessionInfo, package versions and the permutation seed are stored with the results
The report states that enriched terms are hypotheses and that enrichment results depend on the method chosen
constraints: report: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version, annotation_release
report: leading_edge = per significant set
report: enrichment_caveat = method_dependence, stated explicitly
report: enrichment_report = database, version, rank_metric, universe, size_window
Do not present an enriched GO term as a demonstrated mechanism in atopic dermatitis
caveats: If the p-value histogram from T1S1 was irregular, every downstream enrichment result inherits that unreliability and the report must say so
12000 genes is a reduced feature space relative to a full human transcriptome; the universe reflects what was supplied, not everything expressed in skin
